name: Ecosystem Entities, Market and Operations
blurb: Who is doing the work and what the market is doing: companies, people, funding, jobs, news, the historical timeline, and live telemetry on the health of the field.

domains.name: AI Companies
domains.blurb: Every company in the AI ecosystem, classified by type and carrying funding, leadership, products, for-profit status, and patents.

sections.name: AI Company Directory
sections.blurb: Every company in the tools catalog, with what each ships, whether it is a defendant in a tracked lawsuit, and whether it publishes to the MCP registry.

sections.name: Private AI Companies
sections.blurb: Private companies in the directory, from frontier labs to independent giants, with SEC Form D exempt-offering disclosures where they exist. A company here is one verified not to be an SEC registrant.

sections.name: Public AI Companies
sections.blurb: Listed companies whose value turns on AI, with ticker, CIK, filings, leadership, and the products we track. Source: SEC EDGAR.

sections.name: Research Labs
sections.blurb: The organisations doing frontier AI research, grouped by what funds them rather than by reputation.

sections.name: University Labs
sections.blurb: Academic groups producing significant AI research, with institution, principal investigators, and funding.

sections.name: Government Labs
sections.blurb: State-funded AI research and safety institutes, with mandate, budget where published, and leadership.

sections.name: Nonprofits and Open Source Foundations
sections.blurb: Nonprofits and open source foundations stewarding models, standards, and shared infrastructure, with governance model and funding.

sections.name: Funding and Valuation
sections.blurb: SEC Form D exempt-offering disclosures across the directory: what US securities filings actually show was raised, filing by filing. Valuations are not published here because no lawful free source for private valuations exists.

sections.name: Acquisitions and Partnerships
sections.blurb: Who bought whom, and who is tied to whom.

sections.name: Patents
sections.blurb: AI patent filings and portfolio size by company. Source: PatentsView or USPTO.

domains.blurb: Commercial and open source AI products, with pricing, strengths, weaknesses, alternatives, and governance notes.

sections.name: Job Listings
sections.blurb: Open AI roles, by function, seniority, and location.

sections.name: Salary Data
sections.blurb: What AI roles actually pay, by market and level.

sections.name: Skills in Demand
sections.blurb: Which skills employers are hiring for, and how that is changing.

domains.name: The AI Talent Network
domains.blurb: People who work with AI, listed by verified skills: the models, frameworks, vector stores, and governance standards they have real experience with.

domains.name: AI Observatory
domains.blurb: Live telemetry on the health of the field: release cadence, repository activity, uptime, GPU availability, funding, patents, and regulatory movement.

sections.name: Model Release Cadence
sections.blurb: How fast new models are shipping, and by whom.

sections.name: Repository Activity
sections.blurb: This section tracks GitHub star counts and push activity across 55 widely used open-source AI repositories, spanning frameworks like TensorFlow and PyTorch, inference tools like Ollama and llama.cpp, and newer agent projects like AutoGPT and browser-use.

sections.name: Hugging Face Trends
sections.blurb: This section tracks Hugging Face model activity: total download volume across roughly 16,363 tracked models, the most-downloaded individual models, and the license types those models are published under.

sections.name: API Uptime
sections.blurb: This section tracks measured uptime for 12 AI API providers, including Anthropic, OpenAI, Cohere, Groq, Cerebras, Deepgram, ElevenLabs, AssemblyAI, Stability AI, Baseten, Fireworks AI, and Lambda.

sections.name: Cloud GPU and Compute Telemetry
sections.blurb: What can be lawfully measured about AI compute: quarterly capital expenditure from the seven companies whose capex is the buildout, read from their own XBRL facts on SEC EDGAR, plus GPU cloud service health and verified benchmark registries.

sections.name: Funding Activity
sections.blurb: This section is meant to track capital flowing into AI companies by funding stage and sector.

sections.name: Patent Filings
sections.blurb: This section tracks cumulative AI-related patent counts for 108 companies, ranking them by total portfolio size and charting how the combined total moves over time.

sections.name: Security Incidents
sections.blurb: This section tracks open incidents reported on the status pages of 12 AI infrastructure and model providers, including Anthropic, OpenAI, Cohere, Lambda, Fireworks AI, Baseten, Deepgram, and ElevenLabs.

domains.name: Who Works in AI

domains.name: The Art of AI
domains.blurb: Ten creative disciplines and what AI is doing inside each: visual art, film, voice, music, dance, writing, theater, photography, interactive work, and the rights that govern all of it.
